findings.description: The placement check's invocation set is derived by grepping the literal string `stamp-confirmed.sh`, but every script in this smoke test is bound to a variable once and invoked through it — the literal filename never appears on an invocation line anywhere in the file's 1309 lines. So the set the clause calls "every actual invocation" contains, for a house-style artifact, zero invocations and one variable assignment. That produces a false FAIL on correct work and a false PASS on the clause's own named failing example, and which one you get is decided by where the worker puts an assignment rather than by where the tests run.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:458-460 `calls=$(/usr/bin/grep -n 'stamp-confirmed\.sh' ...)` and :457 the comment 'every actual invocation, which is not the same set as every mention'. House style, re-derived at 924f81f: `lint=inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh` at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:11, `vtt=` at :522, `migrator=` at :588, `verify=` at :970; 22 invocation lines go through `"$migrator"`/`"$verify"`/etc. `grep -n 'migrate-scope\.sh'` over the whole file returns exactly two lines, :588 (the binding) and :600 (C-17's require_text). Zero literal invocations exist. Built three synthetic artifacts, each with C-17's wiring require_text inserted beside the `scripts/lint-scope.sh` one at :300. (F) correct section between the guard bounds, invocations via `"$stamper"`, binding at :590 beside `migrator=` — which is where the constitution's own Baseline at :43 and C-17 point the worker: 'snap=587 banner=1299 first-call=590 last-call=1303 cmp=1311' -> OUTSIDE THE GUARD. False FAIL on a blocker. (G) same section, binding moved inside the section: 'first-call=1299 last-call=1299' -> 'inside the guard', but first and last are both the assignment; no invocation was measured. (H) banner and binding inside the guard at :1298-1299, every real `bash "$stamper"` line appended at :1318-1319, after cmp=1304: 'snap=587 banner=1298 first-call=1299 last-call=1299 cmp=1304' -> **inside the guard**. H is verbatim the clause's own failing example at :508, 'a real section, correctly written, appended at :1310 where the fixture guard cannot see it', and the check green-lights it. Prescribed fix verified against all five artifacts: widen the pattern to the binding's variable, `grep -nE 'stamp-confirmed\.sh|\$\{?stamper\}?'`, keeping the three exclusions, and add one clause sentence pinning the variable name to `stamper` and requiring the binding to sit inside the section. Re-ran: B 'inside', D 'inside', G 'inside', F OUTSIDE (now a true FAIL with an accurate diagnosis, since the binding is outside the section), H OUTSIDE (false PASS closed).

C-18 verbatim: exit=0, four lines — 'stamped: _memory/context/atlas-region-topology-mPmy8XBe5H.md 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17', 'stamped: _memory/context/r-nokey.md none -> 2026-02-17', 'skipped: _memory/context/r-proposed.md (status: proposed, not accepted)', 'skipped: _memory/decisions/freeze-window-owned-by-ops-ocPwdpeY0a.md (v1 record, no schema key)' — closing 'stamped: 2  skipped: 2'; the two anchored greps at :640-641 returned **2 and 2** (r4 got 3 and 2 from the bare '^stamped: '), 'insert reported as an insert', `grep -c '^last_confirmed: 2026-02-17' r-nokey.md` = 1, 'proposed record untouched', lint 'failures: 0'. Then rebuilt r4's state-leaking variant: `leaked_cur` outlives its iteration, so a record with no last_confirmed takes the update branch carrying the previous record's value, the substitution matches nothing, and the file is rewritten unchanged while the run reports a stamp. It passes C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6 and C-7 verbatim with output identical to the conforming run. Against C-18 it printed the same counts (2 and 2), the same closing line, the same 'failures: 0' — and 'INSERT REPORTED AS AN UPDATE' plus `grep -c` = 0 on r-nokey.md. C-18 is the only clause in the document that catches it. Also attacked stage 1 with a last-group-wins variant: counts came back 1 and 3 against the stated 2 and 2, caught. The clause earns its length.

The guard message is tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:1300, `  echo "a migration test wrote to a checked-in fixture" >&2` — an echo, so a rewording naming the script by filename is now excluded. findings.description: The contract does not say which spelling of the record path the output lines carry, while C-18's new anchors require relative-to-scope-root. A stamper printing the resolved absolute path is conforming by the contract's own words and fails two clauses with diagnoses that name the wrong thing.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:66-68 pins `stamped: <record-path> <old-or-none> -> <new>` without defining `<record-path>`; :71 says 'sorted by **resolved** record path'; :251 tells the worker that string-equality dedupe fails case 4 and 'one built on `realpath` passes it'. A worker who follows that and prints the realpath is consistent with every sentence in the contract. Built that variant: it passes C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-6, C-7 unchanged, then C-18's `grep -c '^stamped: _memory/'` and `'^skipped: _memory/'` both return **0** against the stated 2 and 2, and C-5 prints 'ORDER DEPENDENT' — not because it is argument-ordered, but because `ab` and `ba` run on `$S` and `$S.b` so the absolute paths differ between the two runs. Two FAILs, neither diagnosis naming the actual problem. One sentence under the output block fixes it: paths are printed relative to the scope root, whichever spelling named them.

findings.description: All seven acceptance criteria map to clauses that would catch their violation. I re-walked each against the shipped document. The C-13 blocker is a defect in one clause's check code, not a coverage gap — but it lands on the one clause that carries AC7 alone.
findings.evidence: spec.md:27-33. AC1 'a confirmation stamps last_confirmed on a v2 record' -> C-1 (ran it), C-6's insertion half (ran it), C-7, C-8 (detection), C-13 (smoke), C-17 (SKILL.md calls it), C-18 (both stamp branches in one run). AC2 'v1 records are skipped and never gain the field' -> C-2 (ran it: 'v1 untouched'), C-13's saboteur (extracted and run: it delegates to the real script and then writes 'last_confirmed: 2026-02-17' onto the v1 record, so a red suite means the v1 hold is asserted), C-18's v1 row. AC3 'every stamped record is named in the verify report' -> C-9's rubric, fed by the contract's per-record output lines at :66-68; C-9 exceeds AC3 by also requiring the declined list. AC4 'no confirmation prompts for per-record approval' -> C-8 ('the resulting stamp does not pass through phase 5'), C-17 (call before phase 5), the contract's 'It writes by default. No `--apply`' at :93, C-10, and C-14's required pass-table row on the absence of any per-record prompt. All judgment, correctly — the absence of a prompt is not scriptable. AC5 'the operating rules name the write-through as the sole sanctioned exception, with its reasoning' -> C-10, VTT collision anchor re-verified at SKILL.md:459. AC6 'a record confirmed twice in one run is stamped once' -> the batch contract at :61, C-5 cases 1-4 (all four ran and all four now discriminate, order-independence included), C-17 requirement 1, C-13's required cross-group smoke assertion, C-18's two-group record. AC7 'the smoke test asserts that a run over the mixed fixture leaves v1 records untouched' -> C-13 alone, with C-2 supplying the content and the saboteur supplying the falsification. AC7 is the criterion the preamble at :7 names as the reason for the script-vs-prose split, and its placement harness is the thing that is broken.
